objective: Empirically qualify the frozen SAFE-A representation, map its real JPEG failure cliff, validate phase/DCT cues and the JPEG inspector on actual project media, and decide whether a tiny SAFE-B head or independent compression specialist is justified.
primaryQuestions: Whether Seedream-4 and Imagen-4 occupy non-real structure in the frozen 512-D representation
Where SAFE-A collapses across actual JPEG tables, encoders, subsampling, and compound transforms
Whether phase/DCT features remain stable and discriminative when SAFE-A fails
Whether deterministic inspector outputs match known bytes and an independent decoder
Whether a frozen-backbone linear head has unique rescue without sacrificing specificity

dataRoles.flux1: consumed diagnostic only; never fitting, threshold design, or independent confirmation

phaseDct.thresholdTuning: none on confirmation; scalar AUC/effect sizes descriptive

safeB.condition: only after descriptive representation analysis shows plausible held-out family separation
allowed: tiny MLP only after predeclared linear-underfit escalation
